data_quality_warning: AoFrio is a distressed micro-cap: FY2025 net debt $8.2m, cash $1.3m, 15-year loss history, and a May-June 2026 capital raise that fell $6.1m short of its $15m target. Base and Bear DCF scenarios below imply equity value at or below zero once net debt is subtracted from a decade of thin projected owner FCF -- the stock's positive market value reflects option value on the IoT/SaaS ramp (SCS 800 / AoFrio iQ) that a discounted-cash-flow model built on realized financials cannot fully capture. Read this DCF as a downside/base-case floor check, not a precise fair-value estimate. Displayed intrinsic values are floored at $0.00 (limited liability); raw (unfloored, potentially negative) values are also reported for transparency.

inputs.post_raise_basis: FY2025 434.232m + May-2026 Wairahi placement 65.135m (NZ$4.559m @ $0.07) + 1-for-7 rights issue ~62.01m shares (implied by $4.341m of the combined $8.9m raised, at $0.07/share, on the pre-placement register) = ~561.4m shares. This is an estimate reconciled against the disclosed $8.9m total raised; exact post-raise register should be confirmed against the next quarterly/annual report.
inputs.net_debt_basis: FY2025: TotalDebt $9.553m - Cash $1.342m = $8.211m. Does not yet reflect any FY2026 raise proceeds retained as cash or used to pay down debt -- next filing should be used to true this up.
inputs.fy2026_basis: 1H26 actual $33.8m (Motors $10.6m, IoT $23.2m) + 2H26 estimate: Motors flat at 1H26's post-customer-loss run-rate (~$10.6m), IoT +5% YoY vs 2H25 (deceleration from 1H26's 6.8% pace). FY2026 total ~$71.1m, -14.5% YoY, consistent with management's Aug-2026 guidance that full-year revenue improvement over FY25 ($83.2m) 'now appears unlikely' and within the analysis brief's -15%/-20% guide range.
inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/annual report cash flow statement (StockBasedComp column, AOF.NZ_Metrics.csv) -- SBC has been consistently negligible for this company (0.02%-0.13% of revenue, FY2021-FY2025), unlike SaaS peers; modeled forward at a flat 0.1% of revenue.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not material -- company holds net debt, not net cash; no interest-income deduction required.
inputs.additional_dilution_mechanism: Base/Bear scenarios model further dilutive equity raises (at a conservative $0.07/share, matching the 2026 placement/rights price) whenever cumulative owner-FCF burn exceeds an assumed $8.9m liquidity headroom (current cash + facility capacity beyond the already-completed 2026 raise). This is funding-driven dilution, not SBC-driven, reflecting the company's realistic path to needing more capital given multi-year negative FCF. Bull case requires no further dilution because it turns FCF-positive within 2-3 years.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs are not usable growth anchors for this DCF. EPS has been near-zero/negative in 6 of the last 8 years (no meaningful compounding to measure); reported FCF was negative in 6 of the last 8 years (FY2018-2025), so no FCF CAGR is computable; equity CAGR is actually NEGATIVE over 3 years (-12.6%) as accumulated losses erode the FY2022 capital raise, and revenue CAGR is dominated by the FY2020 COVID trough base effect (17.7% 5yr) rather than organic strength. None of the standard CAGR anchors are appropriate. This DCF instead builds revenue bottom-up from the realized 1H2026 Motors/IoT segment split and management's FY2026 guidance walk-back, per the analysis brief.
historical_growth.notes: Reported FCF has been negative in FY2018, FY2019, FY2020, FY2022, FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 (6 of last 8 years); only FY2021 (+$1.7m) and the small FY2024 (-$0.14m, near breakeven) were close to positive. FY2025 FCF of -$5.26m was driven by capex ($9.08m, ~10.9% of revenue, mostly capitalized SaaS platform development) outrunning operating cash flow. SBC has never been a material driver of the gap between reported and owner FCF for this company (always <0.15% of revenue) -- the entire adjustment here is about capex intensity and working capital, not stock compensation.

base.narrative: IoT (SCS Connect / SCS 800 / AoFrio iQ) gradually offsets the structurally smaller Motors book; capex stays elevated (capitalized development) then moderates slowly; EBITDA margin climbs from ~2.5% toward ~9.8% by year 10 as mix shifts and opex leverages, tracking below management's own 'self-funded' FY30 target (10% margin at $140m revenue) given the weaker FY26 starting point. One further dilutive raise (~27m shares, ~+5%) assumed to fund the multi-year cash burn before FCF turns durably positive around year 5-6.

bull.narrative: SCS 800 / AoFrio iQ commercial launch converts the 33 active trials into meaningful purchase orders in 2H26 and beyond; Food Retail vertical scales past its first LatAm supermarket order; recurring SaaS mix keeps rising toward the long-stated 50% target. EBITDA margin reaches 16% by year 10 -- still well short of the 'aspirational' $300m/EBITDA $50m (16.7% margin) FY30 target, since that target implies a much faster ramp than modeled here. No further dilution needed; FCF turns durably positive by year 3.

bear.narrative: SCS 800 / AoFrio iQ trials fail to convert to meaningful purchase orders; Motors keeps bleeding share to EMEA competitor pricing with no replacement for the lost US customer; recurring SaaS revenue stays a rounding error. Owner FCF never turns positive within the 10-year horizon (still -$0.8m in year 10) as capex-heavy platform investment outruns a stagnant, low-margin revenue base. Repeated dilutive raises (~205m new shares cumulative, +37% to the post-2026-raise count) required to fund the ongoing burn -- consistent with the going-concern-adjacent risk flagged in the qualitative analysis.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Values floored implicitly NOT applied here (raw values shown) so the reader can see how far below zero base-case equity value sits across the WACC/terminal-growth space; even the most favorable corner (WACC 16%, terminal growth 5%) remains negative (-$0.0006/share).

probability_weighted.weight_rationale: Base gets the largest weight as the most likely trajectory (gradual IoT offset of Motors decline, consistent with management's own 'self-funded' path being more credible near-term than the 'aspirational' path). Bear is weighted above the usual 25% given the crystallized customer-concentration risk, undersubscribed capital raise and thin liquidity -- this is not merely a growth-deceleration bear case but a real going-concern-adjacent scenario. Bull is weighted below its usual 25-30% because it requires the still-unproven SCS 800/AoFrio iQ commercial ramp (first POs not yet booked as of Aug-2026) to succeed at a scale well beyond anything demonstrated to date.

wacc_rationale.rationale: Full risk-premium stack sums to 22.25% (CAPM 12.75% + micro-cap 3.0% + illiquidity 2.5% + customer concentration 2.0% + funding risk 2.0%), reflecting AoFrio's genuinely elevated risk: NZX micro-cap (market cap ~NZ$30-45m), thin trading, crystallized single-customer loss, and a 2026 capital raise that fell 41% short of its $15m target with cash down to $1.3-1.4m. Applied base-case WACC is moderated to 20% (below the full stack) for comparability with similar-risk NZX micro-caps already modeled (AGL.NZ 17%, 2CC.NZ 19%), while still sitting above both as AOF's combination of realized customer loss AND undersubscribed raise AND multi-year negative FCF is a materially worse combination of risks than either comparable. Bull case uses 18% (successful execution reduces funding/concentration risk); bear case uses 23% (funding risk fully realized, approaching distress-level discounting).

sanity_check.basis_note: Multiples computed on SBC-adjusted EBITDA (SBC is immaterial at 0.02-0.13% of revenue for AOF.NZ). P/E unavailable: EPS negative in 14 of 16 years. These will not match screener P/E figures, which use GAAP EPS.

implied_multiples.note: Base-case IV is $0.00 (raw -$0.012, floored at limited liability), so implied multiples are zero. No over-valuation trip is possible; the model errs in the conservative direction.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.outliers_excluded: FY2016-FY2017 EV/EBITDA (470x/84x from near-zero EBITDA denominators) and FY2016 P/B 11.2x excluded from averages; retained in the by-year table for visibility.

sanity_check.price_position: Current price NZ$0.065 sits at the 5th percentile of the 10-year range (NZ$0.056-0.237); at ~561m post-raise shares the market cap of ~NZ$36.5m implies ~1.5x post-raise book and ~0.5x sales -- at or below historical averages, so the market price is not stretched versus history. The gap to the DCF reflects the model's view that the business does not convert EBITDA to owner FCF, not an elevated market multiple.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No fix required. Base and bear scenarios produce negative raw equity value because net debt (~$8.2m) exceeds the base-case enterprise value (~$1.1m); the weighted IV of ~$0.009 is 86% below market. The divergence direction is market-above-DCF, which the Step 8c trip criteria (built to catch over-valued DCFs) do not penalize.
sanity_check.dcf_vs_market_divergence: The DCF's base and bear scenarios imply equity value at or below zero, while the market prices AOF.NZ at ~NZ$36-45m enterprise value (~12.8x FY2025 EBITDA of $3.5m, or ~25x an FY2026 EBITDA estimate of ~$1.8m at a 2.5% margin). This is a genuine and material divergence, not a modeling error: a component-built DCF discounting realized financials at a risk-appropriate 20% WACC cannot capture the option value the market is plausibly pricing into a business with (a) a large, still-unconverted connected-device installed base (3.2m units, $17.8m deferred revenue), (b) a newly launched SaaS platform (SCS 800/AoFrio iQ, 33 active trials) with asymmetric upside if it converts, and (c) strategic/takeout optionality given the tiny market cap. Treat the DCF outputs as a fundamentals-only floor/stress-test, not a complete estimate of fair value -- the bull case ($0.046, still -29% below market) is the closest analogue to what the market may be pricing, and even that requires successful commercial execution not yet evidenced in bookings.
sanity_check.leverage_check: Net debt ($8.2m) alone is roughly 18-23% of the market's implied enterprise value (~$36-45m) and exceeds the DCF's own computed enterprise value in the base case ($1.1m) by more than 7x -- this single fact is what drives base-case equity value to roughly zero and should be the primary risk the reader takes away from this model, independent of any single assumption.
sanity_check.capex_intensity_check: FY2025 capex was 10.9% of revenue (up from 2.5% in FY2021), consistent with the qualitative analysis's warning that capitalized SaaS development is a real, recurring cost. This model keeps capex at 8.5-9.5% of revenue through year 2-3 before moderating only slowly to ~4.6-4.8% by year 10 -- deliberately NOT assuming the recent capex spike evaporates, per the modelling guidance.

valuation_philosophy: Fundamentals-only floor valuation. A component-built owner-FCF DCF on AoFrio's realized financials (15 years of losses, FCF negative in 6 of the last 8 years, capex at ~11% of revenue from capitalized SCS 800/AoFrio iQ development, and the largest US motor customer lost to tariff-driven onshoring in 1H2026) produces negative raw equity value in the base ( -$0.012) and bear (-$0.027) cases, floored at $0.00: net debt of ~$8.2m exceeds the base-case enterprise value by more than 7x. The probability-weighted IV of ~$0.009 versus the NZ$0.065 market price does not mean the market multiple is stretched -- at ~1.5x post-raise book and ~0.5x sales the price is below its own 10-year averages, and the price sits at the 5th percentile of its 10-year range. Rather, the market is pricing option value on the IoT/SaaS ramp (3.2m connected installed base, $17.8m deferred revenue, 33 SCS 800/AoFrio iQ trials with first purchase orders expected 2H26) plus takeout optionality that a cash-flow-only DCF cannot capture. Treat these outputs as a stress-test floor: the bull case ($0.046, still -29% vs market) is the closest analogue to what the market is paying for, and it requires commercial execution not yet evidenced in bookings. An investment case here is a venture-style bet on the SaaS conversion, not a value case supported by current cash generation.
